scenes.headline: How a 320B model runs on a free Kaggle TPU
scenes.sub: GLM-5.3-Flash on eight v5e chips: three-bit experts and a hand-written Pallas kernel.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pompom! Someone put a three-hundred-twenty-billion-parameter model on Kaggle's free TPU. Here's how it fits, and what sets its speed.

scenes.text: Store the experts as roughly 3-bit codebook indices: cheap enough to fit, and expensive to read on every token.
scenes.say: The trick is the weight format. Experts packed as codebook indices, at about three bits, fit on the chips. But they're costly to read back on every token.

steps.note: IQ2_S gate and up matrices sit 25% from bf16
steps.say: The routed experts are ninety-five percent of the model. So they come from Unsloth's GGUF at roughly three bits, repacked into planes a Pallas kernel can read.
Everything else comes from the original FP8 checkpoint, at int8. All told, each chip holds about fifteen gigabytes of its sixteen point nine.
At decode, a fused kernel unpacks each expert inside the matrix multiply, so full-size weights never exist in memory. The README quotes about sixty-four tokens a second.

scenes.title: Per weight, inside the decode kernel

items.say: Each weight is a codebook index, so first, look it up with a lane gather.
Unpack the level and sign bits with shifts.
Convert to float and multiply-accumulate against the activation.
That's about one gather per weight, on the chip's single vector unit, while its four matrix units wait.

scenes.label: for a step's 384 MB of experts at full bandwidth; they take 8.97 ms
scenes.note: arithmetic on three published rates, not a profile
scenes.say: So the limit isn't memory. At full bandwidth, a step's expert bytes would move in under half a millisecond. They take nearly nine.

scenes.text: The codebook format that lets 320B fit on a free TPU is the same format that caps its decode speed.

recap: Experts at ~3 bits: 13.84 GB per chip
A fused kernel unpacks weights inside the matmul
Decode is bound by gathers, not HBM
scenes.say: To recap: three-bit experts that just fit, a kernel that unpacks them in place, and a speed set by gathers, not memory.
